submission.bindingBasis: The owner contract for "exact retry means the same checkpoint and continuity disposition with the same original expectedRevision" — an exact replay is only valid under the stale expectedRevision if we can verify whether the original transition committed. The consequence boundary evidence is outcomeUnknown, so we cannot tell whether the original checkpoint already committed at expectedRevision+1 (which would make REPLAY_EXACT safe) or whether a different actor caused the revision advance (which would make a stale-revision replay conflict).
submission.rationale: We must not guess. The planning-time evidence says the checkpoint commit response may have been lost/ambiguous, and consequenceBoundaryEvidence says outcomeUnknown with ownerChanged (revision advanced). The generic revision signal does not disambiguate whether our original request caused the advance. If it did, REPLAY_EXACT yields admission=existing (safe convergence). If it did not, replaying the same checkpoint at the stale expectedRevision conflicts per the owner contract. Since a wrong choice between REPLAY_EXACT and conflicted stale action depends entirely on an unknown commit outcome, HOLD or blind action risks either forever-deferral or a conflict. REOBSERVE is the only decision that resolves the ambiguity without issuing a different checkpoint or overwriting newer state, preserving the intended convergence goal.
